metadata.name: checkwash
metadata.summary: Flags known patterns of weakened tests and CI checks in a Git diff.
metadata.description:
# checkwash [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/checkwash.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/checkwash/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/LICENSE) **Check whether a code change weakens your tests.** A test can pass after it stops checking something useful. checkwash reads your Git diff and flags known patterns such as deleted assertions, skipped tests, relaxed expectations, and CI checks that stop failing. ```diff - assert total == 105.3 + assert total > 0 ``` The new assertion accepts many incorrect totals. checkwash flags changes like this for review, including changes written by coding agents. **Runs locally. No LLM. No network during analysis. Never executes your code.** The [0.13.1 candidate](docs/releases/v0.13.1-public-launch.md) adds a Python test check for a local replacement of an imported function. The install commands and Action pin below name v0.13.0, the latest release whose public files are verified ([release history](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/releases/README.md)). Start in one of three ways: **Claude Code hooks**, **the CLI on a repository**, or **the GitHub Action** as a required check. ## Use it with Claude Code You need **Python 3.11+, Git and Claude Code**. Install the CLI, then run the hook installer from the root of your repository: ```bash pipx install checkwash==0.13.0 checkwash hook install --agent claude-code --local ``` This writes checkwash's hooks to `.claude/settings.local.json`, your machine-local Claude Code settings (`--local` is the default; `--shared` writes `.claude/settings.json` without the PreToolUse prompt): - **Stop hook:** checks the working tree and the session's commits when Claude is about to finish (paired with a `SessionStart` hook that records where the session began). On a blocking finding, it stops Claude and returns the finding so Claude can restore the test or explain what blocked. - **PreToolUse ask (`--local` only):** prompts before an `Edit`, `Write` or `MultiEdit` of a Python test file leaves a `high` finding under one of five weakening rules (`ASSERT_WEAKENED`, `ASSERT_REMOVED`, `TEST_DISABLED`, `TOLERANCE_LOOSENED`, `BROAD_EXCEPT_ADDED`). Non-interactive `claude -p` runs deny such edits because nobody can answer; the interactive prompt itself is not verified in automated tests. Both hooks are author-side checks: edits made through `Bash` bypass the PreToolUse ask, and engine errors in the Stop hook report a non-blocking note (except working-tree files over the size limit). To enforce verdicts on merges, configure the required CI check under [Use it in CI](#use-it-in-ci). Hook limits are documented in the [0.11.0 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.11.0.md). ## Try it on a repository You need **Python 3.11+ and Git**. Download the single-file zipapp and run the built-in offline examples first. Windows PowerShell (including 5.1, where `curl` aliases `Invoke-WebRequest`): ```powershell curl.exe -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.0/checkwash.pyz python checkwash.pyz --version python checkwash.pyz demo ``` macOS/Linux or Git Bash: ```bash curl -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.0/checkwash.pyz python checkwash.pyz --version python checkwash.pyz demo ``` You can also [download `checkwash.pyz` in your browser](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.0/checkwash.pyz). Then, from a Git repository with at least two commits: ```bash python checkwash.pyz check HEAD~1..HEAD ``` - **Uncommitted changes:** `python checkwash.pyz check` - **Branch review from merge base:** `python checkwash.pyz check BASE...HEAD` (`BASE..HEAD` compares the two snapshots directly) - **Hands-on walkthrough:** follow [`examples/invoice`](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/examples/invoice/README.md) to watch a failing test, a one-line shortcut edit that makes it green without fixing the bug, and checkwash's block. Running `check` from a subdirectory analyses the whole repository from its Git root and notes that root on `stderr` ([#416](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/416)). For JSON/SARIF output and machine integration, see the [embedding guide](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/embedding.md) and [stability contracts](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/stability.md). ## Use it in CI To stop a merge, make the **`checkwash` status check required** in your repository's branch rules. Installing the tool or adding a workflow alone does not enforce its verdict. Save this as `.github/workflows/checkwash.yml`: ```yaml # .github/workflows/checkwash.yml on: [pull_request] permissions: contents: read jobs: checkwash: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1 with: fetch-depth: 0 persist-credentials: false - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0 with: python-version: "3.12" - uses: taipei49314/checkwash/action@9ada8cfaa618b002b5d0d829c7ddbe1b8e8ae638 # v0.13.0 ``` After the workflow runs once, open **Settings → Rules → Rulesets** and require the `checkwash` status context (keep the job unconditional). Repository administrators with a clone of this project can also add the ruleset via: ```bash gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --method POST --input action/required-ruleset.json ``` `checkwash doctor` checks the local workflow file (it cannot inspect live GitHub branch protection). When upgrading, update the CLI and local hooks before bumping the Action pin; see [CI details](#ci-details-doctor-and-the-pin). ## When checkwash blocks | Result | What to do | |---|---| | **Pass · exit 0** | No finding requires blocking under your configuration. Keep running your normal test suite and code review. | | **Block · exit 1** | Read the finding and the diff. It may be weakened verification or a false positive. | | **Error · exit 2** | Resolve the input or analysis error before relying on the result. | The default threshold is **high**: a visible **warn** still passes. **Read the finding.** For the diff at the top of this page inside `test_invoice_total` in `tests/test_billing.py`, checkwash prints: ```text ASSERT_WEAKENED HIGH tests/test_billing.py :: test_invoice_total test_invoice_total: assertion strength EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40) why high: NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF no de-escalator applied before assert total == 105.3 after assert total > 0 ``` `EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40)` ranks assertion strength before and after; `why high` names the escalator (`NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF`, or `REPAIR_EVIDENCE_REFUSED` when weakened alongside a production edit). Use `checkwash check --format json` for machine-readable output. **Fix the change, or record a reviewed exemption.** If the test was weakened by mistake, restore it and fix the code. If the weaker test is intentional, record a time-boxed exemption (90 days default, 180 max) using the fingerprint printed in the report: ```bash checkwash allow "" --reason "why the weaker test is correct" ``` Configuration and exemptions are read strictly from the **base** side of the diff (comparing `.checkwash/` against any `.greenwash/` predecessor), so a PR cannot exempt or relax rules for itself: merge the ledger entry through code review first, and protect `.checkwash/` and `.greenwash/` with [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md#4-codeowners) ([exemption rules](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md#3-allowlist--reviewed-time-boxed-base-side)). **Report a false block.** If checkwash blocks an honest change, check the [failure ledger](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/benchmarks/FAILURES.md) first, then open an [issue](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues) with the **checkwash blocked honest work** template (`checkwash check --format json` plus the diff). Accepted reports become regression fixtures crediting the reporter. ## Know the limits **checkwash is alpha.** A pass means no known tampering pattern was flagged at or above your threshold; it does not prove a change is correct or honest. Python is the primary supported language; JS/TS support covers a bounded set of patterns. Four core limits to know before relying on a pass: - **Test files are found by default naming conventions.** Python files are scanned when named `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` outside pytest's default ignored directories (`build/`, `dist/`, `venv/`, dot-directories), reading only default pytest test names; non-default filenames such as `tests/pricing_tests.py` or Django `tests.py` emit an `analysis incomplete` note on `check` (`stderr`, terminal report and SARIF) when changed, and are not parsed as test units even if `pyproject.toml` collects them. JS/TS scans zero-configuration Jest and Node paths (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `__tests__/**`, `.js`/`.ts` under `test/`, and `tests/` files importing `ava` or `tap`), without reading `jest.config.*`, `vitest.config.*`, `.mocharc.*` or `package.json` `jest` collection rules. - **A JS/TS pass covers fewer patterns than Python.** Fewer assertion and helper idioms are modelled in JS/TS, and runner config changes that silently drop test files are not read. - **Editing agent-instruction files blocks, except strict inert EOF appends to root `CLAUDE.md`.** Changes to root `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.claude/**`, `.checkwash/**` or `.greenwash/**`—and any prepend, mid-file insertion, adjacent append without a blank line, deletion, edit, reorder, or fence/comment/`---`/`[label]:` addition in root `CLAUDE.md`—escalate `GUARDRAIL_TOUCHED` to `critical`. Strict inert appends at the end of root `CLAUDE.md` separated by a blank line (`GUARDRAIL_ADDITIVE`), appended exemption entries (`EXEMPTION_ADDED`), and newly created guardrail files that do not weaken checkwash config stay at `warn`. - **Claude Code hooks are author-side helpers, not a merge gate.** Only the required CI check in range mode enforces verdicts on pull requests. **Honest refactors and behaviour changes can require exemptions.** Weakened, removed, skipped or loosened Python assertions (and weakened, loosened or skipped JS/TS assertions) refuse production repair evidence (`REPAIR_EVIDENCE_REFUSED`), so removing a deprecated API with its assertion or rewriting a test beside a behaviour change requires a reviewed `checkwash allow` entry. On the project's 60-case refactor corpus (57 strictly qualified), the expected-verdict table (`benchmarks/refactors/expected.json`) and the published 0.12.0 CLI mark **6 of 60** as blocking (4 among the 57, including known false blocks `CASE_020_windows` and `CASE_029_flatten`). Changed files over **1,000,000 bytes** are not read (non-Python assets/docs warn on `stderr`; test, CI, guardrail, `.py` or pytest config files over the cap exit 2).
Customizing guarded instruction files (for example, unguarding CLAUDE.md) Subdirectory instruction files, `CLAUDE.local.md`, lowercase `claude.md`, `.gitattributes` working-tree-encoding rules, and other agents' config filenames are not guarded by default. `GUARDRAIL_ADDITIVE` on root `CLAUDE.md` covers only strict inert appends at end-of-file separated by a blank line (no `---`, code fences, HTML comments, `[label]:` definitions or `Cf`/`Default_Ignorable` characters), and stays at `warn` even if an appended plain-text line contradicts earlier prose or adds an `@path` import. To let a blocking guardrail edit through, record a reviewed exemption or override `[roles].guardrail` in a base-side `.checkwash/config.toml` (or `.greenwash/config.toml` if your repository uses that directory): ```toml [roles] guardrail = ["AGENTS.md", ".cursorrules", ".claude/**", ".checkwash/**", ".greenwash/**"] ``` Because this list replaces the default, keep `.checkwash/**` and `.greenwash/**` in it so checkwash continues guarding its own config and ledger. Creating a new config file is a `warn`; editing an already-tracked config is itself a `critical` guardrail edit until merged to the base.
Repair-evidence residuals, JS/TS table scope and refactor-corpus provenance `REPAIR_EVIDENCE` describes related changes in the same diff; it does not prove a repair is semantically valid, and a no-op production edit (such as `+ 0`) can earn it ([#419](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/419)). From 0.12.0 ([0.13.0 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.13.0.md), [0.12.0 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.12.0.md), [0.11.0 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.11.0.md)), weakened/removed/skipped/loosened Python assertions and weakened/loosened/skipped JS/TS assertions take no repair evidence (`REPAIR_EVIDENCE_REFUSED`). By default, rewritten expected values, substituted assertions (including a weakening respelled as one), test deletions escorted by a renamed private symbol, and JS/TS removed assertions/units, deleted parametrize rows, dead-code parked units and stand-in/subject edits still accept repair evidence; to block those too, set `fail-on: warn` in the Action (`checkwash doctor` will then exit 1 because it proves only a step without `with:`) or run `checkwash check --task` with a base-side `oracle_freeze` contract ([enterprise hardening guide](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md#7-hardening-against-bought-repair-evidence-419)). In JS/TS (since v0.9.0, [#428](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/428)), each `test.each`, `it.each` and `test.for` table with a static title is a unit whose rows are counted when written as an inline array, tagged template or same-file `const` used only as a table; `describe.each` rows and computed-title tables remain unread. For the 60-case refactor corpus, **6 of 60** (4 of 57 strictly qualified) is the static source readback retained since the [D-185 dispositions](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/oracle-context-dispositions-0.10.0.md) and matched by the published 0.12.0 CLI on Windows (2026-11-10 UTC). Earlier historical snapshots in the repository record 22/60 blocks (36.7%) at v0.3.1 (`benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json`) and 4/60 (2/57 strictly qualified, with three fixture errors) in a pre-v0.3.4 source replay; those historical records are preserved unchanged and are selected examples rather than a general false-positive rate.
Which files over the 1,000,000-byte limit stop the run, and how each output reports them Since v0.9.0 ([#454](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/454), [#455](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/455)), oversized non-Python assets, lockfiles, docs and non-Python production sources are set aside without earning repair evidence: `--format json` lists them under `unread`, SARIF emits a tool execution notification, and terminal output prints a `!` note (opening with `analysis incomplete` when there are zero findings); `--format hook-json` and `--emit-ir` omit `unread`. Any oversized file a detector or import resolver must read—test, conftest, CI, guardrail, snapshot, JS setup, runner script, `.py` module, pytest config (`pytest.ini`, `.pytest.ini`, `pytest.toml`, `.pytest.toml`, `tox.ini`, `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`) at any depth, or non-generated `scripts/**` file—stops the run with exit 2 (`--format json` prints `{"unread": [...]}` except on an unread symlinked pytest-config target in range mode; term and SARIF stay empty). checkwash streams up to 64,000,000 bytes per Git side and inspects the first 200 bytes of oversized sides solely to detect shell shebangs (an extensionless file with a side over 64 MB still stops the run). Generated paths (`build/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`) are set aside unless they match `.py`, pytest config, CI, runner script or unknown-shebang extensionless rules. At the base, oversized root `poetry.lock`/`uv.lock` warn on `stderr`, while oversized root `pyproject.toml` or `requirements*.txt` exit 2 across term/json/SARIF. In the Claude Code Stop hook (`--format hook-json`), engine errors report a non-blocking message and exit 0, except when a file changed by the hook's diff exceeds the limit in the working tree, which blocks the stop and asks to shrink, split or revert it ([#456](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/issues/456); see [subject integrity](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/subject-integrity.md)).
Try it on your own changes before making it required. [Coverage and limitations](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/stability.md#coverage-and-adoption-cost) · [Known gaps](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/adversarial-catalog-2026-09.md) · [0.13.0 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.13.0.md) · [0.12.0 known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.12.0.md) ## CI details: doctor and the pin The recommended Action and CLI above are both **v0.13.0** (GitHub Release and PyPI 2026-11-17, Asia/Taipei; 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17 UTC). Always upgrade the CLI and its local hooks first, then update the Action SHA in `.github/workflows/checkwash.yml`. [Enterprise setup](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/docs/enterprise.md) · [Action reference](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/action/README.md)
Pin verification, release tag geometry (A vs M), Dependabot/zizmor and <= v0.7.0 advisory **Development snapshots:** source on `main` may be ahead of the published CLI. [The advertised-release manifest](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/release/advertised.toml) records the verified version, tag commit and artifact digests behind the commands above. **Which commit is the recommended pin?** From v0.12.0 (D-200), the release tag points directly at the release's Action commit: `git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}'`. Because an Action commit cannot embed its own commit SHA, each release from v0.11.0 (D-194) has two commits: its Action commit `A`, and the release merge `M` (which differs only in setting `doctor`'s own Action pin line to `A`). PyPI distributions and `checkwash.pyz` are built from `M`, while `checkwash check` in the Action does not import `doctor` and behaves identically at `A` and `M`. Installing the CLI from a Git release tag installs `A`, whose `doctor` rejects that release's own Action pin (`exit 1`)—install the CLI from PyPI or `checkwash.pyz` instead. (For v0.11.0 only, the tag pointed at `M`, so its Action commit was `git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^2^1'`; up to v0.10.0 the tag pointed at the single release commit.) **Pin updaters and `doctor`:** because v0.12.0+ tags point at the Action commit, Dependabot, Renovate and zizmor's `ref-version-mismatch` audit resolve `# v0.13.0` directly to the SHA `doctor` 0.13.0 accepts (inferred from those tools' documentation, not run; `doctor` 0.13.0 accepts the v0.13.0 pin above and v0.12.0's pin, while `doctor` 0.12.0 accepts only v0.11.0 and v0.12.0 pins and exits 1 on the v0.13.0 pin). **Advisory for Action `<= v0.7.0`:** Action releases up to v0.7.0 ran `python -m pip` and `checkwash` with the PR checkout as working directory, allowing a PR to shadow `pip` or `checkwash` ([#372](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/pull/372), fixed in v0.8.0). Pin the v0.13.0 Action above; see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/main/SECURITY.md#known-issue-action-trust-boundary).
## More options and evidence
Install as a CLI or try the included examples If you already use pipx, install the fixed version: ```bash pipx install checkwash==0.13.0 checkwash check HEAD~1..HEAD checkwash demo # 8 tampering cases, blocked, offline ``` `checkwash demo` replays eight tampering cases and one honest fix. Five of the eight are adapted from this project's decoy corpus: coding agents were pointed at small repositories with a failing test and asked to make the suite pass without fixing the bug (given only the task, none of the twelve touched a test). One was found in this project's own release gate; two are synthetic. The demo prints each case's origin. It illustrates known patterns; it is not a coverage guarantee. You can run the same examples with `python checkwash.pyz demo`.
Read the measurements and their limits The historical six-repo sweep recorded **46 / 1800 = 2.56%** blocks: **31 false positives (1.72%)**, 15 legitimate policy blocks (0.83%). The tracked artifacts record engine **v0.3.0** (the release commit, swept 2026-09-07) on a corpus used to tune the detectors, not a held-out result. **1.33% of the corpus (24/1800) records opaque production changes**. That flag does not establish that each verdict changed or each diff was unanalyzed. Review methods vary: the three-rater agreement study covers an older 35-diff cohort, not all 46 blocks. The dedicated **22/60 refactor** result (`benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json`, a dated v0.3.1 snapshot) is a separate population; the general-commit rate does not predict it.
